mcqs.title: Interpreting dimensions
mcqs.stem: After a default CSV import, movies.shape is (2228, 11). What does this tell you?

options.text: There are 2,228 movies and 11 data columns; the row index is not one of the 11 columns.
There are 2,228 movies and 10 data columns plus the row index.
Only the 5 rows shown by head() were imported.

mcqs.rationale: shape reports data rows and columns, excluding the index.

mcqs.title: Selecting a variable
mcqs.stem: You assign ratings = movies['IMDB Rating']. Which description is correct?

options.text: ratings is a two-dimensional DataFrame with 11 columns.
ratings is a Python list without row labels.
ratings is a one-dimensional Series that retains the corresponding row labels.
ratings is the mean rating as a single number.

mcqs.rationale: Selecting one named column with a single pair of brackets produces a Series.

mcqs.title: Diagnosing an import
mcqs.stem: A text file header is Title;Year;Rating. Reading it with the default pd.read_csv() returns one column named Title;Year;Rating. What is the best next step?

options.text: Use head(3) to split the column into three variables.
Read it again with sep=";", then inspect its shape and column names.
Rename the file to .csv; pandas will then infer three columns from the extension.
Use index_col=0 to separate the three variables.

mcqs.rationale: The semicolon delimiter must be parsed; a successful function call alone does not prove the table was read correctly.

mcqs.title: Preserving the intended columns
mcqs.stem: movies has a default RangeIndex containing only row numbers. You want a CSV with its existing data columns and no extra row-number column. Which export fits that goal?
mcqs.rationale: index=False omits the row index; meaningful IDs stored in an index would need to be preserved when required.

rubric.evidence: 1 point: correct CSV import and requested previews; 1: correct shape/column evidence; 1: observation, variables, and index interpretation.

1 point: dtypes and info output; 1: non-null count interpreted against total rows; 1: describe output with correct rating mean and median; 1: Series type/shape and explanation; 1: head limitation and attribute/method distinction (0.5 each).
1 point: raw preview and prediction; 1: default-import evidence interpreted; 1: correct explicit separator and successful import; 1: dimension/column comparison with CSV.
1 point: export with index=False and successful reimport; 1: visible structural checks interpreted; 1: default-row-number prediction and meaningful-ID explanation (0.5 each).
0.5 point: name and organized code, outputs, and Markdown; 0.5: completion note describing fresh run, save, and HTML inspection. HTML alone does not prove execution history.
